candidates.name: how-to-scrape-viator-in-nodejs
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js example (4 commits, last touched ~16 Mar 2026, 1 star) that calls the Apify 'Viator Scraper' actor to pull Viator tour listings — names, URLs, thumbnails, per-person price + currency, availability dates, location, rating and review count. Includes a sample-output.json showing the shape but no bulk committed dataset; real pulls land in Apify's own dataset store (paid actor runs) and would need to be re-run.
candidates.why_useful: A working, documented one-command method to pull live Viator (Experiences competitor) tour pricing/availability/review-count by destination — could proxy activity demand/pricing for gap #9 (competitor supply) if run repeatedly at named cities; not itself a stored panel.
candidates.time_coverage: point-in-time snapshot per run, no history stored
candidates.size_hint: sample JSON only; real pulls depend on Apify actor runs (paid)

candidates.name: Viator-and-GYG-Scraper

candidates.why_useful: Potential dual-source (Viator + GetYourGuide) activity scraper; unverified — code and output format not confirmed, flag for a closer look rather than trusted as a working source.

candidates.name: getyourguide-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Single-commit scraper for GetYourGuide tour reviews: tour URL/activity name, reviewer traveler-type tag (e.g. 'Family with young children'), star rating, full review text, review date; handles pagination; exports to JSON/CSV/Excel/HTML. No dataset committed — it is an extraction tool, 0 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Review text + dates on a competitor Experiences marketplace could feed a demand/sentiment nowcast for tours & activities (adjacent to Airbnb Experiences), similar in spirit to the reviews-based 'stays index' already built for Inside Airbnb.
candidates.time_coverage: reviews carry their own posted dates; pull is current-state only

candidates.name: viator (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Independent third-party documentation of Viator's public API surface (Viator is owned by Tripadvisor; largest tours/activities/experiences marketplace) — OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs, auth, error codes, changelog, LLM/MCP tool defs. No data, no code beyond machine-readable API descriptors. Points to Viator's own official API docs as the real source.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Viator exposes a documented OCTO-standard REST API (auth required, presumably needs a partner key) — useful as a map for anyone building a legitimate, TOS-compliant pull of Viator activity/pricing data rather than scraping.
candidates.license: unclear (API Evangelist's own repos are typically CC/MIT for the meta-docs; underlying API is Viator's own)

candidates.name: getyourguide (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Same API Evangelist format as the Viator entry, profiling GetYourGuide's public API surface for tours/activities/attraction tickets booking (Berlin-based OTA). Spec files and metadata only, no data.
candidates.why_useful: Maps GetYourGuide's official API as an alternative to scraping for a legitimate activity-pricing/availability pull; low value on its own.

candidates.name: klook (API Evangelist profile)

candidates.why_useful: Confirms Klook (APAC things-to-do platform) exposes an OCTO-standard partner API; a map toward legitimate APAC activity-market data rather than a data source itself.

candidates.name: tripadvisor (API Evangelist profile)

candidates.why_useful: TripAdvisor's official Content API covers hotel reviews, attraction/experience listings and location data across cities globally — this repo is only a map to it, but is a lead toward a legitimate cross-city review-volume/rating panel spanning hotels AND experiences, which nothing in our current holdings covers jointly.

candidates.why_useful: Very marginal — no persisted dataset described, scraping logic buried inside a chatbot app; would need code inspection to extract the scraping piece.

notes: The WebSearch tool returned 'session has used its web search budget (200 of 200)' on the very first call — evidently a session-wide (not per-agent) quota already exhausted by other concurrent scout agents before this scout ran. Fell back to WebFetch against github.com/search (client-rendered, returned false '0 results' and frequent HTTP 429), Bing and DuckDuckGo (DDG served a CAPTCHA on every query, Bing returned no github.com results for these travel-brand queries), and finally the unauthenticated GitHub REST search API (https://api.github.com/search/repositories), which worked but rate-limits hard (~1 request per 10-15s before 403) — had to pace calls with sleep. This theme (Viator/GetYourGuide/Klook/Airbnb Experiences) has almost no substantial GitHub data presence: no repo found with a committed CSV/Parquet dataset of tour/activity listings, prices, or bookings from any of these three OTAs. What exists is (a) small, mostly unmaintained/undocumented scraper repos for Viator, GetYourGuide, and Klook (0-1 stars each, several with no visible README), and (b) the api-evangelist GitHub org's uniform 'independent third-party API profile' repos, which document each platform's official public API surface (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs under the OCTO tours-and-activities standard) but contain zero actual data — useful only as a map toward a TOS-compliant partner-API pull, which per repo rules 6/7 would need human sign-off before running. Also found via the same org: tripadvisor, oystercom-tripadvisor, siteminder (hotel distribution/channel manager), thefork and bookatable (restaurant reservations, tangential), restorando, housetrip (defunct vacation-rental competitor), listings-api. None of these carry data. Did NOT find: any Airbnb Experiences-specific dataset, scraper, or API client (Airbnb has never published an Experiences partner API, unlike Viator/GYG/Klook which follow OCTO); any 'hotel-on-Airbnb' (Airbnb's hotel-room inventory push) dataset or tracker; any academic replication package on tours/activities pricing. Suggest a future pass specifically search GitHub Code Search (not repo search) for filenames/strings like 'viator.com' + '.csv', 'octo' + 'tours', or the OCTO standard's own reference-implementation repos, and check Kaggle/Zenodo directly (outside GitHub) since this vertical seems to have essentially no open GitHub data footprint — the real data (if it exists at all) likely lives behind paid scraping-as-a-service platforms (Apify store, Bright Data, ScraperAPI 'Viator/GetYourGuide' marketplace listings) rather than in public git repos.
